Stated Claim / Post Context:
500 new members by the new year

Keep our people-powered D.C. news going strong into 2027!

Actual Article Body:
D.C. needs artists who remain connected to the city, so we can preserve things that money, development, and time can’t recreate. Here are some tips to keep you here.

Domestic violence survivors, among others, say the process at DHS’s Virginia Williams Family Resource Center “feels like it’s designed to break you down when you are at your lowest point.”

While supplies last!

Keep our people-powered D.C. news going strong into 2027!

Two and a half years ago, The 51st was just an idea. Our vision was bold: What if we created a newsroom where the workers shaped its future, where the community we covered felt genuinely represented, and where we were beholden only to our readers, not wealthy shareholders or a billionaire owner? And you — our neighbors — stepped up.  Now we need your support again! To keep our work sustainably funded through 2027, will you help us reach 500 new members by December 31? All support is tax-deductible!

In our two years of existence we’ve gone from having zero full time employees to having seven, along with five dedicated part-time workers. We’ve contributed to a Pulitzer Prize winning series, we’ve translated our articles into Spanish and Amharic, and we published a voter guide that was read by over 50,000 people — that’s one-third the total number of voters in the recent historic primary.

Being predominantly reader-funded allows us to produce journalism that is sustainable, independent, and unafraid. Will you become a member so we can continue to report news that makes your lives better?

Workplace and institutional support:

Supporting The 51st isn't just for individuals! We've heard from a few readers wondering if their workplace could buy a subscription for all employees (how fun!), or if their business could become a sponsor (how cool!). We're finally able to say: YES!

We also accept workplace matching gifts for employee donations. All of these options contribute to this campaign! EIN 99-3371005.

It's no surprise that funding for local news has shifted drastically in the last decade, and we're committed to finding creative and values-aligned ways to grow and sustain our newsroom, by D.C. for D.C.

If you're a paid subscriber, please share why YOU supported this campaign in the comments! ⬇️

Put simply, our mission is to make it easier — and more fun — to live in the District. Our members help keep local news free and independent for all:
